spec.description: A camera crossing Paris, one picture a second, and what it has in sight at each: the street ahead worked out against the buildings, beside the picture it took, the landmarks on the ground it sees, and everything it has seen so far.

spec.rawSql:
-- Where the camera is at the Time Brush's instant.
SELECT epoch_ms(time) AS "Time", distance_m / 1000 AS "Ridden", speed_kmh AS "Speed"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')
WHERE time <= coalesce(nullif($t1, ''), '2025-05-13T12:41:45.000Z')::TIMESTAMP
ORDER BY time DESC
LIMIT 1

spec.description: Where the camera is at the Time Brush's instant: the clock in Paris, how far it has gone from Port-Royal and how fast it goes.
spec.title: At the instant

spec.rawSql:
-- Overture's places on the ground the camera sees now ($visible, written by the map's Viewshed
-- layer), widened by about 10 m: a shop's point lies inside its building, never seen itself.
SELECT count(*) AS "Places in sight",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE category IN ('monument', 'historic_site', 'christian_place_of_worship', 'religious_organization', 'museum', 'theatre_venue', 'movie_theater', 'public_plaza', 'park', 'bridge', 'public_fountain', 'sculpture_statue', 'library', 'college_university', 'science_attraction') AND confidence >= 0.9) AS "Landmarks in sight"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/places.parquet')
WHERE confidence >= 0.6
  AND nullif($visible, '') IS NOT NULL
  AND ST_Within(ST_Point(longitude, latitude),
                ST_Buffer(ST_GeomFromText(coalesce(nullif($visible, ''), 'MULTIPOLYGON EMPTY')), 0.0001))

spec.description: Overture's places on the ground the camera sees now, within a few metres; the landmarks among them are listed below.
spec.title: In sight now

options.content:
**Where it comes from.** A camera on its way across Paris on 13 May 2025, from Port-Royal to Strasbourg-Saint-Denis by Boulevard Saint-Michel, Pont Saint-Michel, the Île de la Cité, Pont au Change, Châtelet and Boulevard de Sébastopol: 626 pictures in 15 minutes, one a second, each with its time, its place, the way the camera looked and its speed. Pierre Beyssac took them and shared them on [Panoramax](https://panoramax.fr), the open street-level imagery of OpenStreetMap France and IGN (CC BY-SA 4.0); your browser reads each picture from Panoramax. The places are [Overture](https://overturemaps.org)'s (release 2026-10-21.0) within 300 m of the route. Pacha reads both into files once (`datasets/paris-ride/build.sh` in pacha-dashboards).

**How a view is worked out.** By the Kepler Plus map's Viewshed layer, in the browser, at each picture: lines of sight from 1.5 m above the street over a grid of cells about two metres across, 300 m ahead in the camera's 76° field of view, turned the way it looked, against the buildings of the base map (OpenStreetMap's, as OpenFreeMap serves them, with their heights) on flat ground. A cell is coloured when the street there, at ground level, can be seen. The layer writes that ground to the dashboard (`$visible`), and the places in sight are Overture's places on it.

**What it leaves out.** Trees, buses, parked vans and people in the way, which the picture shows; buildings OpenStreetMap draws without a height count as 15 m. A tower or a spire shows from farther than its foot.

spec.rawSql:
-- The camera's speed, picture by picture: the Time Brush plays the ride.
SELECT time, speed_kmh AS "Speed (km/h)"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')
ORDER BY time

spec.description: The camera's speed through the ride. Press play: the window grows from the start, and the maps, the picture and the lists follow its end. Drag the end to go to a moment.
spec.title: Play the ride: 15 minutes across Paris

spec.rawSql:
-- The landmarks the camera has in sight now (monuments, churches, museums, theatres, squares,
-- bridges, fountains, colleges) Overture is sure of (confidence 0.9 or more), nearest first: Overture's places on the ground it sees ($visible,
-- written by the map's Viewshed layer), widened by about 10 m.
WITH cam AS (
  SELECT latitude AS clat, longitude AS clng FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet') WHERE time <= coalesce(nullif($t1, ''), '2025-05-13T12:41:45.000Z')::TIMESTAMP ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1
)
SELECT place AS "Place", replace(category, '_', ' ') AS "Kind",
       round(2 * 6371000 * asin(sqrt(pow(sin(radians(latitude - clat) / 2), 2)
             + cos(radians(latitude)) * cos(radians(clat)) * pow(sin(radians(longitude - clng) / 2), 2)))) AS "Metres"
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/places.parquet'), cam
WHERE confidence >= 0.9 AND category IN ('monument', 'historic_site', 'christian_place_of_worship', 'religious_organization', 'museum', 'theatre_venue', 'movie_theater', 'public_plaza', 'park', 'bridge', 'public_fountain', 'sculpture_statue', 'library', 'college_university', 'science_attraction')
  AND nullif($visible, '') IS NOT NULL
  AND ST_Within(ST_Point(longitude, latitude),
                ST_Buffer(ST_GeomFromText(coalesce(nullif($visible, ''), 'MULTIPOLYGON EMPTY')), 0.0001))
ORDER BY "Metres"
LIMIT 40

spec.description: The monuments, churches, museums, theatres, squares, bridges and fountains on the ground the camera sees now, nearest first (Overture's places, widened by about 10 m: a building's point lies inside it). A tall one, a tower or a spire, shows from farther than its ground: it is listed only once its foot is in sight.
spec.title: Landmarks in sight

spec.rawSql:
-- The picture the camera took at the Time Brush's instant (its window's end), and where it was.
-- The browser reads the picture from Panoramax: a small copy while the instant moves, the large one
-- once it rests.
SELECT picture_id, photo, replace(photo, '/sd.jpg', '/thumb.jpg') AS thumb,
       strftime(time + INTERVAL 2 HOUR, '%H:%M:%S') AS clock,
       round(speed_kmh) AS speed, heading, round(distance_m / 1000, 2) AS km
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')
WHERE time <= coalesce(nullif($t1, ''), '2025-05-13T12:41:45.000Z')::TIMESTAMP
ORDER BY time DESC
LIMIT 1

spec.description: The picture the camera took at the Time Brush's instant, as Panoramax keeps it (faces and number plates blurred). Pierre Beyssac took the ride's 626 pictures on 13 May 2025 and shared them under CC BY-SA 4.0.
spec.title: What the camera saw

spec.rawSql:
-- The camera's pictures, one a second: where it was, which way it looked and how fast it went.
-- The Time Brush above moves the map's time window; the camera is where its last picture in the
-- window was, gliding between two.
SELECT camera, time, latitude, longitude, heading, speed_kmh
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')
ORDER BY time

-- The whole route as one line, with no time: the map always draws it.
SELECT 'Port-Royal to Strasbourg-Saint-Denis' AS route,
       'LINESTRING (' || string_agg(longitude || ' ' || latitude, ', ' ORDER BY time) || ')' AS _geojson
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')

spec.description: The camera 1.5 m above the street, following it, and the ground it has in sight within 300 m ahead (yellow, fading with distance): its 76° field of view, turned the way it looked, against OpenStreetMap's buildings. The street ahead that it cannot see is shaded. Worked out in the browser at each picture, between two the camera glides. Play the ride in the Time Brush above.
spec.title: What the camera sees

spec.rawSql:
-- Every other picture, for what the camera has had in sight since the start: each one a view
-- of its own, the ones in the time window together.
SELECT camera, time, latitude, longitude, heading
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')
QUALIFY row_number() OVER (ORDER BY time) % 2 = 1
ORDER BY time

-- The whole route as one line, with no time: the map always draws it.
SELECT 'Port-Royal to Strasbourg-Saint-Denis' AS route,
       'LINESTRING (' || string_agg(longitude || ' ' || latitude, ', ' ORDER BY time) || ')' AS _geojson
FROM read_parquet('http://feeds/datasets/paris-ride/ride.parquet')

spec.description: Every other picture from the start to the Time Brush's instant, each with its view: the union of the ground the camera has had in sight within 300 m on its way, in blue. Streets it crossed without looking down them stay blank.
spec.title: Everything it has had in sight so far
Across Paris: what the camera sees
